title: Kingdom of Powys Wenwynwyn
capsule: Powys Wenwynwyn was the southern portion of the Welsh kingdom of Powys, separated c. 1160 when Owain Cyfeiliog took the southern lands centered on Welshpool (Pool) and his nephew Owain Brogyntyn held the north as Powys Fadog. The kingdom takes its name from Gwenwynwyn ab Owain (r. c. 1195–1216), who mounted the last significant Welsh resistance in the region before submitting to King John of England. After Gwenwynwyn's death the line survived as marcher lords under English suzerainty, the family progressively assimilated into the English peerage through the later 13th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's approximate territory in southern Powys is derivable from Welsh chronicle sources and English administrative records, but its boundary with Powys Fadog is approximate.
